newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian minister criticised over homosexuality.
newsitem.headline: Belgian minister criticised over homosexuality.

text.p: Belgian Deputy Prime Minister Elio di Rupo, under investigation following under-age sex allegations, came under fire on Monday for his previously hidden homosexuality.
Charles Ferdinand Nothomb, chairman of the francophone Christian-Democrat PSC government party, was quoted as saying that a minister could not be openly homosexual.
"I have problems with anyone who is an apologist for homosexuality," Nothomb was quoted as saying in Belgian media.
Belgium's parliament asked the country's top court last Thursday to investigate allegations that Di Rupo had sex with boys younger than 16, the country's age of consent. A report is due by Monday.
Di Rupo, a discreet homosexual, has denied the allegations, and several newspapers have seriously questioned the reliability of the sole witness who has testified against him.
The chairman of his francophone Socialist Party PS backed Di Rupo and said he should keep his job while the court investigated. But he ducked questions about Nothomb's statement.
"The PS reiterates its confidence in its deputy prime minister," Philippe Busquin told a news conference on Monday.
On Friday, two Flemish newspapers questioned whether a homosexual could hold a ministerial post.

"The number two in the government is a 45-year-old man who ...frequents night-time bars, seeks relations with socially weak youngsters and avoids questions about their age. Even if they are not minors, the question remains whether such a man can represent the country and the king," daily De Standaard wrote.
Marc Platel, editorialist of Flemish daily Het Belang van Limburg, said on Friday politicians should behave "decently".
"By visiting certain circles or bars...public figures are vulnerable to blackmail, regardless of whether they are homosexual or heterosexual," Platel said.
The Belgian parliament on Monday released details of the allegations against Di Rupo.
"Statements made to the prosecutor could indicate a possible crime by (di Rupo)...If these facts proved to be true, they could be described as rape of a minor," the report said.
Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene last week accused the prosecutor of not vertfying the authenticity of the allegations before making his report to parliament.
